200.description: Bootstrap config; update.decision is none|recommended|required, where required comes from updatePolicy.minSupportedVersion or from a mandatory active release. wallet.tokens lists the token catalogue for the app (BootstrapWalletToken[]): only enabled tokens on the tenant's enabled chains, tenant rows override global rows with the same (chain, address), sorted by sortWeight DESC then symbol ASC; it never carries verified/id/scope (the app grants verified from its own allowlist). wallet.tokens is required by the app schema; every enabled chain carries an enabled native entry, and every delivered row is validated before delivery (a corrupt row makes the whole bootstrap fail with 503 rather than being repaired on the read path); services.predict (domain, scopeId, chain) is present only while modules.predict is enabled and is 503 when enabled but not configured. Optional installation authentication: a request carrying X-Installation-ID plus Authorization: Installation <credential> is matched against canary releases, so the device may receive update.full/update.ota for a canary build instead of the active one; an absent, expired or revoked credential is treated as anonymous and only ever sees active (bootstrap itself never fails on a credential problem). update.canary.enrolled says whether the offered full release is a canary build; update.canary.otaToken is a 24h opaque token that the app must store with Updates.setExtraParamAsync("canary-token", token) so the native manifest request can be matched to a canary OTA revision (the key must stay lowercase: expo-structured-headers rejects uppercase dictionary keys). otaToken is null when the installation could not be authenticated, and the app then clears the stored param. update.minSupportedVersion and the mandatory flag always come from the active release, never from a canary one features.directUpdateEnabled is additionally false when the requesting build and the release it would install were signed with different certificates (the platform installer would reject the in-app install after the download), so the client falls back to opening the download URL instead of looping a failing install.

503.description: BOOTSTRAP_UNAVAILABLE: the tenant configuration, its token catalogue or its wallet section could not be produced completely (storage error, a corrupt catalogue row, an enabled chain without a native token, or a tenant whose configured chains are all unknown). The app keeps its last successful snapshot and shows the retry screen

The certificate carries X509v3 Key Usage: Digital Signature and Extended Key Usage: Code Signing, which is exactly what expo-updates' CertificateChain checks; NotBefore is backdated five minutes because the client validates against the device clock. An OTA job is refused when the tenant has no OTA signing key, when the base release carries no runtimeVersion, or when another OTA job for the same tenant and platform is still in flight (OTA_BUILD_ALREADY_QUEUED) - the queue is shared across tenants and OTA jobs have no build-number monotonicity to limit them. channel is never taken from the request: it is compiled into the base APK, so it comes from the tenant's composed identity. post.description: Same certificate, new recipients: a key is only sealed when it is generated or imported, so a signing gate added later never receives it, and generating a new key would change the certificate (installed apps could not upgrade). The primary decrypts its own box, seals the same plaintext to the recipients it trusts locally (itself, trusted signing gates the server reports as active with matching fingerprints, trusted unrevoked recovery keys) and signs keystorebox.ResealMessage(resealId, upload). One transaction with build.keystore and release.android locked: the caller must be the active routed primary; the tenant must have a usable v3 keystore at keystoreVersion; no pending generation (it replaces the recipients anyway); certificate, package name, key alias and tenant slug must equal the current record; the signature is verified with the registered Ed25519 key; recipients must all be registered, include the primary's own accepted X25519 key and at least one unrevoked recovery key. Writes build.keystore (sealKind=reseal, generator, generationSignature, generationRequestId=resealId), leaves release.android untouched, audits build_keystore_resealed with the added and removed recipients. A retry with the same resealId and signature returns 200 without writing. Which recipients are added is decided on the signing gate: the server cannot add a key the gate does not trust locally.

post.summary: Claim a build to sign
post.description: Only the active primary signer gets jobs (anyone else: 204). Candidates are, for every tenant named in the ready list, its apk job in built that is the lowest build number among the tenant's in-flight jobs (queued, claimed, running, built, signing) for that platform (at most one per tenant, no page limit, so tenants that cannot be dispatched never starve the others); a candidate is dispatched when whose tenant is ready (same judgement as SIGNER_NOT_READY) and for which the ready list contains an item exactly equal to the server's (tenantSlug, packageName, certificateSha256, trustRootsDigest). Claiming happens under the release sequence lock (the same lock as manual uploads and completions): if the platform already has a release whose version or build number is not lower than the job's (a manual upload while the job was still queued or building), the job is failed on the spot instead (failure_reason explains it, audit build_job_sign_overtaken) and not dispatched. Otherwise claiming increments signAttempt, deletes any signed package left by a previous sign attempt and moves the job to signing. keyAlias and trustRoots are for comparison only. A job this signer deferred (POST /jobs/{id}/release, signOutcome.kind=deferred with this machine's id) is not dispatched to the same signer again until 60 seconds after signOutcome.at; other signers are not affected.

post.summary: Complete signing: create the release and finish the job atomically
post.description: Outside the transaction the server reads the signed package back from storage (the key recorded by the last signed upload of this claim) and runs the same release checks as a manual upload: signer certificate = registered keystore certificate = certificateSha256, package name, versionName/versionCode = job, not the public debug key, not a retired certificate; unsignedSha256 must match the builder delivery and nativeFingerprint must equal the value from the builder's verified provenance (422 SIGN_RESULT_MISMATCH otherwise; the package does not carry it, so the release records the job's value with file_metadata.nativeFingerprintSource = builder-provenance). The signing heartbeat is refreshed before the download so a long verification is not reaped. Then, under the release sequence lock, one transaction locks the job row, checks status/signAttempt/machine, checks that the signed object key is still the one that was verified (409 SIGNED_ARTIFACT_REPLACED when the package was uploaded again meanwhile: call complete again) that the signer has not been revoked meanwhile (401 MACHINE_REVOKED), and re-reads release.android and build.keystore with a shared lock: if the registered package name, certificate or keystore changed after the verification the completion is refused (409 RELEASE_IDENTITY_CHANGED, audited as release_rejected; call complete again), checks that version and build number increase, inserts app_releases (status verified, file_metadata adds unsignedSha256, sbom, nativeFingerprint, nativeFingerprintSource, commitSha, commitSelfReported, buildJobId, builderId, signerMachineId), marks the job succeeded with release_id and artifact_sha256, and audits as system-signer. Idempotent: a succeeded job with the same signed sha256, the same signAttempt and the same signer machine returns the same releaseId; the same signer and attempt with a different signedSha256 gets 409 SIGN_RESULT_CONFLICT (the recorded release is not replaced); any other signer or attempt gets 409 SIGN_ATTEMPT_STALE. Exempt from the database timeout by exact route match.

reportedTrust.description: Signers only: what this signer's local record trusts, as it last reported (POST /v1/signer/keystore-checks trust). Display only (e.g. the primary does not trust the standby yet, so new keys will not be sealed to it); signers never take it from the server. null = not reported: never reported, or the latest report came from a signer version that does not send trust.

reportedTrustAt.description: When reportedTrust last changed; null while reportedTrust is null

os.description: Operating system of this machine; always present, defaults to linux for machines registered before this field existed. Decides which bundle it installs.

name.description: Builders: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$. Signers additionally at most 22 characters (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,21}$): a signer runs as the system user rn-signer-<name>, and Linux user names are limited to 32 characters. Only checked on create; machines registered earlier keep their names.

os.description: Operating system of this machine; omitted = linux. It decides which bundle it installs (linux/amd64 or darwin/arm64) and which installer script the console shows. A darwin machine must be a builder that can build ios; the signing gate is Linux only.

publicKeySha256.description: Full 64-hex sha256 read on the machine itself (colons and upper case accepted)

ed25519PublicKeySha256.description: Required when the machine is a signer (400 INVALID_MACHINE without it): the full 64-hex sha256 of the signer's Ed25519 key read on the signer itself (colons and upper case accepted), which must equal the pending Ed25519 key (409 MACHINE_KEY_MISMATCH). Checking only the X25519 fingerprint would let a stolen token pair the real X25519 key with a foreign Ed25519 key while the machine is pending. Builders have a single key: leave it out (any value is 409 MACHINE_KEY_MISMATCH).

keyAlias.description: For comparison only; the signer uses the alias inside the box

publishedMaxBuildNumber.description: Largest build number among this tenant's Android release records (0 if none)

generator.description: The primary signer that generated the current keystore, as registered when it delivered it; null for imported keystores (confirm them with signer confirm)

upload.description: The whole current upload file, when generator is not null (a standby verifies the generation signature over it)

recipients.description: Every recipient fingerprint of the current keystore (sorted), null when there is no box. The primary compares it with the signing gates and recovery keys it trusts locally and reseals the same certificate when one is missing (POST /v1/signer/keystore-reseals).

sealKind.description: How the current keystore was stored, when generator is not null: generation (keystorebox.GenerationMessage) or reseal (keystorebox.ResealMessage, same certificate, new recipients). Records from before reseals read as generation.

items.description: One item per tenant with a keystore sealed to this signer, plus (for the active routed primary) tenants with a pending key generation. An item that only carries a generation request (new tenant, legacy record, or a keystore not sealed to this primary) has box, packageName, certificateSha256 and keyAlias null; keystoreVersion is the current build.keystore row version (0 if none), and its trustRoots are composed with the requested package when the tenant has no release identity yet. Do not report checks for such items.

localRole.description: This signer's role according to its own local record (signer promote/abandon). Required on every report. Stored on the machine as reportedLocalRole/reportedLocalRoleAt, written only when it changes; a routed primary whose reportedLocalRole is not primary makes tenants not ready (PRIMARY_SIGNER_LOCAL_ROLE_MISMATCH).

trust.description: Sent on every report by current signers: the signers (including this one), builders and recovery keys this signer's local record trusts. Stored on the machine as reportedTrust/reportedTrustAt (build_machine_trust_report audit), written only when it changes. Optional for signers released before the automation (they do not know the field): a report without trust (or with trust null) is accepted as usual - localRole and the items are recorded - and sets reportedTrust and reportedTrustAt to null, meaning this signer version does not report its trust (not 'trusts nothing'); the console shows it as not reported. Nothing but console hints reads reportedTrust, so signing and readiness do not depend on it.

items.description: Check results only for keystores sealed to this signer; items for other tenants, other keystore versions or keystores without a box for this signer are ignored.

nativeFingerprint.description: Must equal the nativeFingerprint of the builder's verified provenance recorded on the job

SignerReadinessProblem.description: One reason the primary signer cannot sign for this tenant yet. code is a fixed enum the console maps to a fix-it entry; detail is a human sentence that may name a machine or quote the signer's error. KEYSTORE_NOT_CONFIGURED: no build.keystore. KEYSTORE_LEGACY_FORMAT: build.keystore is a pre-signing-gate record (v1 passphrase box or v2 build-agent box); reset and upload v3. KEYSTORE_RECORD_INVALID: build.keystore is a v3 record that cannot be used (the record is malformed, the outer box cannot be opened, or its index fields differ from the stored upload); the keystore view still reports configured=true, the queue gate answers SIGNER_NOT_READY and the signer keystore checks omit the tenant - upload the v3 file again. RELEASE_IDENTITY_NOT_CONFIGURED / RELEASE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH: release.android is missing or differs from the keystore's package name or certificate. PRIMARY_SIGNER_MISSING: no active primary signer is registered. PRIMARY_SIGNER_NOT_RECIPIENT: the v3 keystore has no box for the primary signer. PRIMARY_SIGNER_LOCAL_ROLE_MISMATCH: the primary signer in the console has never reported its local role or its local record still says standby (it was not promoted on the machine), so it will not claim jobs; promote it on the machine or switch the console back. APP_IDENTITY_INCOMPLETE: tenant.json cannot be composed (missing app parameters, bootstrap signer address, release identity). OTA_CERTIFICATE_NOT_CONFIGURED: no ota.signing, so trust roots cannot be composed. API_BASE_URL_INVALID: the stored apiBaseUrl is not a canonical https origin (e.g. an explicit :443 saved before write-time validation). TRUST_ROOTS_INVALID: the composed trust roots do not normalize (e.g. scheme http/https). PRIMARY_SIGNER_NOT_CHECKED: the primary has not reported a check for the current keystore version. PRIMARY_SIGNER_DECRYPT_FAILED: its trial decryption failed. PRIMARY_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIRMED: not confirmed on the machine (signer confirm). TRUST_ROOTS_CHANGED: confirmed, but with a trust roots digest that is no longer current. PRIMARY_SIGNER_TRIAL_SIGN_PENDING / PRIMARY_SIGNER_TRIAL_SIGN_FAILED: the trial signing has not passed yet / failed. The last three only appear while the tenant has no usable v3 keystore (they explain why there is no key yet; a tenant with a usable key keeps signing with it while a replacement is generated): RECOVERY_KEY_NOT_CONFIGURED: the platform has no unrevoked offline recovery key, so no key can be generated. KEYSTORE_GENERATION_PENDING: a generation request waits for the primary signer. KEYSTORE_GENERATION_FAILED: the latest generation request failed; detail carries the signer's code (e.g. TRUST_ROOTS_CHANGED, RECOVERY_KEY_NOT_PINNED, PEER_NOT_TRUSTED), KEYSTORE_GENERATION_STALE or KEYSTORE_GENERATION_TIMED_OUT (pending for more than 30 minutes).

tenantDirectory.description: Directory under RN-App tenants/ (build.android repoDirectory, defaults to the slug)

tenantFile.description: tenant.json composed by the server for this job: slug, appName, scheme, androidPackage, iosBundleId, apiBaseUrl, bootstrapSignerAddress, applicationId, distributionChannel, otaChannel, version, androidVersionCode, iosBuildNumber, iconBackgroundColor, icon{icon,androidForeground,androidBackground,androidMonochrome}, signerSha256

icons.description: Icon file names to fetch one by one with GET /v1/build-agent/jobs/{id}/icons/{name}

googleServicesJson.description: base64 google-services.json, or null when not configured

otaCertificatePem.description: Public OTA code-signing certificate compiled into the package (null when ota.signing is not configured); the private key is never sent

runtimeVersion.description: OTA jobs only: the base release's runtimeVersion

claimedMachineId.description: This builder's machine id; use it as the provenance builderId

attempt.description: Send it as x-build-attempt on every /jobs/{id}/* request

BuilderClaimResponse.description: A claimed job. No keystore material of any kind is included.

MachineEnrollment.description: Returned only by the create and reissue responses. The server stores only the code's sha256; it is valid for 60 minutes and for one enrollment.

installCommand.description: The one-line command to run as root on the new machine, composed by the server from the request's external origin: curl -fsSL <origin>/v1/machine-setup/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --server <origin> --code <code>; signers additionally end with ' --recovery-sha256 <从密码管理器粘贴恢复公钥指纹>' where the angle-bracket placeholder is kept verbatim for the operator to replace from the password manager. Show and copy it as is.

SignerReportedTrust.description: The trust lists in a signer's local record, including the signer itself. Stored sorted; written only when it changes.

name.description: Relative path inside the archive (no absolute paths, empty, . or .. segments); signer unit templates contain @, e.g. templates/rn-signer-@INSTANCE@-check@.service

bundle.description: From manifest.json (rn-machine-bundles/v1) of the deployed bundle directory. install.sh verifies the archive and every file against these sha256 values; with --expect-sha256 it also compares archiveSha256 with the value from the CI log.

recoveryKeys.description: Signers only (empty for builders): the unrevoked recovery keys. signer enroll pins the one whose sha256 the operator pasted (--recovery-sha256).

primarySigner.description: Standby signers only: the active routed primary's accepted keys, trusted on first use by signer enroll to verify the primary's generation signatures. null otherwise.

os.description: Operating system of this machine, from the registry entry.

x25519PublicKey.description: Signers: base64 std of the 32-byte X25519 key. Builders: must be null.

ed25519PublicKey.description: base64 std, 32 bytes. Signers: the record-signing key. Builders: the provenance key (stored as the machine's publicKey).

token.description: The long-lived machine token. Appears only in this response; the server stores its sha256. The enroll command writes it straight into the env file and never prints it.

RecoveryPublicFile.description: recovery-public.json written by the offline tool (build-keystore recovery-key create), signing/recovery.PublicFile.

status.description: Derived on read with the server clock: a pending request whose build.keystore or release.android version changed since it was made is reported as failed with error.code KEYSTORE_GENERATION_STALE; one still pending more than 30 minutes after requestedAt (the primary signer is offline, not upgraded, or the trust roots cannot be composed) is reported as failed with error.code KEYSTORE_GENERATION_TIMED_OUT and can be requested again. completedAt stays null until a late delivery or failure report writes the derived failure back.

code.description: What the primary signer reported (TRUST_ROOTS_CHANGED, RECOVERY_KEY_NOT_PINNED, NOT_LOCAL_PRIMARY, PEER_NOT_TRUSTED, GENERATION_FAILED, …), or KEYSTORE_GENERATION_STALE / KEYSTORE_GENERATION_TIMED_OUT derived by the server

SignerGenerationRequest.description: Only sent to the active routed primary signer while the request is pending. trustRoots are what a first generation for this package trusts (auto:first-generation); a signer that already confirmed the package with a different digest refuses (TRUST_ROOTS_CHANGED).

publishedMaxBuildNumber.description: Largest build number among this tenant's Android release records (0 if none); the first-signing versionCode cap is this + 100 when the signer has no local history

signature.description: base64 std Ed25519 signature by the primary's registered key over "rn-keystore-generation/v1\n" + requestId + "\n" + UploadDigest(upload) (keystorebox.GenerationMessage)

code.description: At least TRUST_ROOTS_CHANGED, RECOVERY_KEY_NOT_PINNED, NOT_LOCAL_PRIMARY, GENERATION_FAILED

keystoreVersion.description: The build.keystore row version this reseal is based on

resealId.description: Chosen by the signing gate; stored as generationRequestId

signature.description: base64 Ed25519 signature over keystorebox.ResealMessage(resealId, upload)

allowUnconfirmedSigners.description: Generate even though a signing gate that holds the current key has not confirmed this version yet (otherwise 409 KEYSTORE_SIGNERS_NOT_IN_SYNC). Those gates then need a manual signer confirm before they can use the new key: a standby only auto-accepts a key that supersedes the certificate it currently holds.

issuerId.description: App Store Connect issuer id (UUID), public information

keyId.description: App Store Connect key id (10 characters), public information

privateKey.description: The AuthKey_<KeyID>.p8 contents, raw PEM or base64. Stored encrypted with STORAGE_MASTER_KEY and never returned

AppleTeamReport.description: One Apple Developer Team a Mac builder reports it can sign for: the Distribution certificate is in its keychain, provisioning profiles for these bundle ids are on disk and the upload key for that team is present. Self-reported and only narrowing: it is an operations dashboard, not a security boundary - whoever holds the machine token can claim to hold any team.

bundleIds.description: Bundle ids this machine has a usable provisioning profile for

expiresAt.description: RFC3339 expiry of the earliest certificate or profile of this team; omitted when unknown

uploadProbe.description: Result of the read-only probe the machine ran at startup against this team's upload key (GET /v1/apps/{id}/buildUploads?limit=1). ok = the key can use the Build Uploads endpoints; forbidden = the role is not enough, swap this machine's key for an App Manager team key; error = the probe could not run. Omitted when the machine does not upload. Known before the first build, rather than after a build number has been burned.

commitSha.description: Commit the Mac checked out. Self-reported: the server has no GitHub credentials to verify it.

ipaSha256.description: sha256 of the .ipa the builder holds. Self-reported evidence of what was built, not a distribution credential - the package users install is the one Apple re-signed.

bundleId.description: Read out of the exported package on the Mac; must equal the tenant's release.ios bundleId.

shortVersion.description: CFBundleShortVersionString; must equal the job's version.

buildNumber.description: CFBundleVersion; must equal the job's build number.

uploadedToAppStoreConnect.description: Whether this attempt actually uploaded the build.

uploadedByEarlierAttempt.description: The upload was skipped because App Store Connect already has this build number - a requeued job keeps its build number, so an earlier attempt may have uploaded a package built from a different commit. Recorded in file_metadata so nobody reads commitSha/ipaSha256 as describing what is on Apple's side.

toolchain.description: The xcodebuild -version line of this Mac, for spotting version drift across the pool.

BundleSignature.description: The offline signature over a bundle manifest. A platform admin signs it on an offline machine with the release key; the server never holds that private key. The machine checks the signature, that the sequence is not lower than one it already accepted, and that the commit equals the approved one, before it replaces any binary.

commit.description: The commit these bundles were built from. A -dirty build cannot be signed.

sequence.description: Raised by one per signature. A machine refuses anything below the highest it has seen, so whoever breaks into the server cannot roll a machine back to an older version that was once legitimately signed. Rolling back on purpose means signing a higher sequence that points at the older commit - an explicit, signed act.

publicKeySha256.description: Which release key signed it; every machine pins one out of band at installation time.

signature.description: base64 ed25519 signature over a canonical line-per-field payload, not over the JSON.
